admissionRules.title: Every measured value cites evidence
admissionRules.description: Any fact stating a business measurement carries at least one evidence identifier that resolves to a record in the snapshot. The two exceptions are the reporting window and the source-coverage line, which describe the briefing itself rather than the business, and are substantiated by the connection list shown beside them.

admissionRules.title: A change needs both periods
admissionRules.description: Movement is stated only where a current and a prior value both exist. A single value is reported as a level, never as a trend.

admissionRules.title: Invalid and stale records are refused
admissionRules.description: Records marked invalid or stale are excluded outright. Partial records may be used, but only with their coverage note carried into the briefing as a caveat.

admissionRules.title: Rates need a denominator worth dividing
admissionRules.description: Percentages and rates built on fewer than 100 denominator events are excluded, because the movement would be an artefact of the sample rather than a finding.

admissionRules.title: Explanations travel as hypotheses
admissionRules.description: A suggested explanation is admitted only where the underlying opportunity records one, and it is carried with the confidence held in it. Where no explanation is supported, the absence is recorded rather than filled in.

admissionRules.title: No overall verdict
admissionRules.description: The packet holds no fact summarising performance as a whole. There is no composite score, no overall grade, and no sentence that averages unlike metrics into a single direction.

sections.title: What the rules flagged
sections.purpose: Deterministic observations raised against this window, with no cause asserted.

facts.statement: AC repair page sessions increased while confirmed bookings and booking rate declined.
Organic sessions rose materially while confirmed bookings from organic search rose far less, so the channel converted a smaller share of the visitors it earned.
Organic sessions increased while GBP profile views, website clicks, and call clicks declined.
The average rating of new reviews declined and at least three permitted excerpts share a scheduling theme.
Search impressions and clicks increased with a modest CTR gain and improved average position.
LinkedIn impressions rose sharply while the share of viewers who engaged fell, which is what usually happens when distribution widens faster than the content resonates.

sections.title: What happened after earlier work
sections.purpose: Measured differences following completed work, with confounders named.

facts.statement: After Water-heater comparison guide refresh, GSC clicks moved from 2,040 in March 2026 to 2,510 in April 2026 (+23.0%).
facts.caveat: Subsequent performance improvement. ReachOps does not attribute causation from this observation alone. Competing explanations on record: The refresh published on 14 March, so the baseline month contains roughly two weeks of post-refresh traffic. That makes the measured improvement conservative rather than inflated.

facts.statement: After AC repair page FAQ, GSC clicks moved from 3,680 in June 2026 to 4,420 in July 2026 (+20.1%).
facts.caveat: A rise that coincides with a seasonal peak is not evidence the work caused it. Treat this as unresolved rather than successful. Competing explanations on record: July is the peak cooling month in Denver. Website sessions across the entire property rose 11.9% over the same two months without any change to those pages. The FAQ published on 15 July, leaving only half the follow-up month exposed to it.

boundaries: No sentence asserts that a recommendation caused a measured change. Work and movement are reported separately, and where both are shown the competing explanations are named.
No sentence reports a figure that is not in the snapshot, and no figure appears without the evidence identifier it came from.
No sentence grades overall performance, assigns a composite score, or states a confidence percentage in its own analysis.
No sentence describes a movement as good or bad on the sign of the number alone; direction is derived from whether the metric is one the business wants lower.
